children.subject: The storefront GraphQL order configuration item exposes five fields and drops productId, quantity and sectionId
children.question: Which configuration item fields does the storefront GraphQL order projection expose compared with the cart?
children.body: The configuration a buyer assembled is not exposed on the storefront GraphQL order in the shape it had in the cart. CartConfigurationItemType has eight fields -- id, name, type, customText, files, productId, quantity and sectionId. OrderConfigurationItemType has five: id, name, type, customText and files. productId, quantity and sectionId are all dropped, and selecting productId, quantity, sectionId, sku, catalogId, categoryId or imageUrl on OrderConfigurationItemType is refused by validation error. So for a configuration section whose type is 'Product', this projection of the order gives the chosen option's NAME and nothing that identifies the product it was or how many were taken, and it does not give which section the choice answered. Anything reconciling a configured order back to catalog products through this projection has only a display string to match on. This is read off the deployment's own schema: read the same two type tables on any deployment and a diff either confirms it or retires it.

children.subject: The stored order keeps the configured product and quantity; only sectionId is lost between cart and order
children.question: Does the stored order record keep the product and quantity chosen in a configuration?
children.body: The stored order keeps the product and the quantity of a configuration: GET /api/order/customerOrders/{id} returns, per Product-type configuration item, productId, sku, quantity, imageUrl, catalogId and categoryId alongside name and type, so the order does identify the catalog product that was chosen and how many were taken. In the modules' own swagger, CartConfigurationItem carries 16 fields and OrderConfigurationItem 15, and the only field the crossing loses is sectionId. The loss of product and quantity is in the storefront GraphQL read surface, not in the record.

children.subject: A store's stock is read from its main fulfillment center, and stock elsewhere leaves the product at zero
children.question: Which fulfillment centers' stock counts toward a store's product availability?
children.body: Stock counts for a store only on the store's own main fulfillment center; stock written to another fulfillment center leaves the product at zero for that store. Disputed by a later observation: a product whose only inventory record (inStockQuantity 2, reserved 0, Enabled) sits on a fulfillment center that is in the store's additionalFulfillmentCenterIds but is not store.mainFulfillmentCenterId was returned by UCP search_products with availability.available_quantity 2 and is_in_stock true. So 'only the main fulfillment center counts' does not hold as stated; the zero-stock case is more likely stock on a fulfillment center that is not assigned to the store at all, neither main nor additional.

children.subject: Purchase requests turn uploaded order documents into a quote and have no approve or reject step
children.question: What does the purchase requests feature do, and does it have approve or reject mutations?
children.body: The storefront's /account/purchase-requests is served by the AI document processing module: a buyer uploads order-like documents (PDF, image, even handwritten) and the pipeline turns them into a quote. The xAPI flow is createPurchaseRequestFromDocuments, then extractPurchaseRequestSourcesData (OCR and line extraction), then postProcessPurchaseRequestSources (catalog matching, which sets quoteId), then normal quote acceptance; there is no approve or reject mutation - buyer approval belongs to quote requests at /account/quotes. The module is flagged experimental.

children.subject: A master product page's variant picker never makes it purchasable, even with every option chosen
children.question: Does selecting every variant option on a master product page make it purchasable?
children.body: Not necessarily. On /products-with-options/configurable-caps-shirts/hat ("Men's Adjustable Scholarship Hat Team Color", advertised as 6 variations, From $4.00) the PDP renders four variant groups - Color, size_shirts, Size_chart, Fabric (data-test-id="variant-picker--<group>--<value>"). Picking a Color alone re-renders the H1 to a concrete variation name ("Light Brown Clemson Hat"), proving the picker does resolve a product, yet the Price stays "N/A" and the add control stays a DISABLED button whose accessible name is "Select options to proceed" - and it still does after one value is selected in ALL FOUR groups (Brown / 55 / No size / Cotton). No option is ever disabled or greyed as unavailable, so the UI gives no way to tell a valid combination from an invalid one; the offered matrix is 6x4x5x4 = 480 combinations against only 6 real variations.

children.subject: Variations are reachable only through their own SEO slug, not search or category listings, and order lines link to the master
children.question: How can a shopper reach a specific product variation, and where does its order line link?
children.body: Variation names are NOT in the storefront search index (searching "Light Brown Clemson Hat" returns no results), and variations do NOT appear as their own cards in their category listing (Configurable caps & shirts shows 6 results, all masters/configurables/simples, none of the hat's variations). What DOES work is the variation's own SEO slug, e.g. /products-with-options/configurable-caps-shirts/brown-vt-print-hat, which shows a real price ($8.99), real stock (3249) and a working quantity stepper. An ORDER line for a variation links back to the MASTER's slug (/products-with-options/configurable-caps-shirts/hat), which is a reliable way to tell a variation line from a simple-product line on an order.

children.subject: Inviting a member immediately provisions a contact and a locked account that Admin shows with an empty Status
children.question: What does a pending invitee look like in Admin right after the invitation?
children.body: Inviting a member creates BOTH a contact and a security account immediately, and the account already carries the role chosen in the invite dialog - the invitation is not a queued message, it is a provisioned account that cannot yet be used. On the Admin account blade the same person shows Locked state = Locked and a Status field that is EMPTY, rendering as the 'Select ...' placeholder. So a pending invitee and a blocked member are both simply 'Locked' in Admin, and the field that could tell them apart is blank for the invitee. Do not read a Locked account as evidence that someone was blocked: check the contact's own status, where a pending invitation reads Invited and a block reads Locked. Disputed in part: an invited account observed after a Block-then-Unblock cycle held zero roles, while another invited row did carry its role, so whether the account keeps the role chosen in the invite dialog is not established.

children.subject: The storefront roster shows a pending invitee as 'Invite sent' with status Invited

children.body: On the storefront roster the row of a pending invitee shows the literal name 'Invite sent' with an empty real name, the chosen role, the email lowercased, and status 'Invited' - so the status column does have a third value beyond Active and Blocked. Disputed on another build: a row rendering 'Invite sent' had a full name in the organization-contacts response, so the page substitutes 'Invite sent' over a name the API supplied, and it showed the green Active badge rather than Invited, because the Active column consumes statusInOrganization and the effective-status fallback materialises a null status as Approved; that row did show its role.

children.subject: Block then Unblock on the roster moves a pending invitee out of the invited state without any mailbox
children.question: Can a pending invitee be moved out of the invited state without completing registration?
children.body: Completing the registration clears the lockout, but it is not the only way out of the invited state, and a deployment with no reachable mailbox can still move a member out of it from the storefront side: Block user followed by Unblock user on the roster row does it. contact.status goes Invited -> Locked -> Approved, Unblock resets the account lockoutEnd from 9999-12-31 to 0001-01-01, emailConfirmed stays false, and the roster afterwards reports the person as Active; Admin then shows Locked state Unlocked and Status PendingApproval. The account's passwordHash reads null through GET /api/platform/security/users/{userName}, which strips the field, but is populated through GET /api/members/{id} on the same invited account, so the two endpoints redact differently.
